subject: Proposal: tiered remit window, credit corridor & VAT handling for PulseHealth
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: tiered remit window, credit corridor & VAT handling for PulseHealth

Hi Lena —

Great speaking yesterday. Per our conversation I put together a pragmatic invoicing/credit approach that should align to PulseHealth's procurement cycle while protecting both sides during the pilot and early ramp. High-level proposal (details attached):

- Pilot payment structure: 30% upfront deposit at SOW signing, 40% at 30 days, remaining 30% at 60 days (Net60 maturity for last tranche).
- Ongoing terms post-pilot: Net45 standard for recurring consumption. We can offer Net60 for the first two billing cycles post-pilot subject to a $250k credit corridor and a credit review at 90 days.
- Credit corridor & limits: $250,000 starting cap; discretionary increase after 90-day review based on usage and payment history.
- VAT / EU handling: Redwood will issue VAT invoices to PulseHealth's EU subsidiary when we have the VAT number on file. For UK/EU reverse-charge scenarios we will include the necessary declarations. If PulseHealth wants consolidated billing at the US entity, we’ll need a W-9 and tax treaty documents.
- Early-pay discount: 1.5% on invoices paid within 10 days.

I attached the draft SOW and a redline of our MSA showing invoicing schedule language. If this looks close, I can route these to finance/ops for final credit paperwork and get DocuSign links ready.

Next step: can you confirm the VAT number for the EU entity and whether procurement will accept the staged deposit model? Also confirm whether procurement prefers Net60 on pilot invoices (we can accommodate but it reduces the initial credit cap to $200k unless we receive the deposit).

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0196

Subject: Re: Proposal: tiered remit window, credit corridor & VAT handling for PulseHealth

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear plan and the SOW. A few clarifications from procurement / finance side:

1) Pilot terms: Procurement prefers Net60 for pilot invoices due to our monthly close cadence. We can do the 30% deposit, but the remaining tranches would be Net60 for consistency.
2) Credit limit: Our finance team is requesting a $300k credit line to cover potential usage spikes in month 2. Is that achievable if we provide trade references?
3) VAT: PulseHealth EU (VAT ID GB123456789) will require standard VAT invoicing. We are a UK-registered entity and will handle reverse-charge where applicable. Please confirm Redwood's VAT registration number so we can validate.
4) Attachments: procurement asked for a sample invoice and the expected invoice remittance details to include in their AP system.

If you can confirm the VAT number and credit process, we can accelerate review on our side.

Best,

Lena Torres
Head of Procurement, PulseHealth

Marissa / Ben —

Looping you both in. PulseHealth (EU/UK) wants Net60 for pilot invoices and is asking for a $300k credit line. They will provide VAT ID GB123456789 and can share trade refs. Procurement also asked for a sample invoice/remittance details.

Proposed internal approach:
- Approve Net60 for pilot only if we take 30% deposit at signing (this preserves cashflow).
- Offer $250k starting cap with the option to increase to $300k after we receive two trade references + deposit (or immediately to $300k if finance signs off).
- Require standard trade credit form and KYC; run Experian/credit check.
- For VAT: provide Redwood VAT reg: GB987654321 (confirming we are VAT registered in UK/EU). We will issue VAT-bearing invoices to their EU subsidiary and include reverse-charge wording where required.

Marissa — can you draft the sample invoice and remittance stub for procurement? Ben — can you confirm whether finance is comfortable with credit checks then immediate bump to $300k upon trade refs, or whether we need to hold at $250k until 90-day payment history?

Thanks,

Jordan

Hi Lena —

Thanks for the quick response and for sharing the VAT ID. Confirming the points below so procurement has a single note to attach to the PO:

- VAT registration: Redwood VAT ID GB987654321 — we will issue VAT invoices to PulseHealth EU (GB123456789) and include standard reverse-charge language where appropriate.
- Pilot invoice cadence: we can accept Net60 for the pilot remainder tranches provided PulseHealth supplies the 30% deposit at signing. Note that Net60 on pilot invoices reduces our initial credit cap; to reach $300k starting credit we need either two trade references (on file) or a co-signed guarantee. Otherwise we start at $250k and re-evaluate after 90 days.
- Credit & collections: Redwood requires a signed credit application (I attached the link below), and we will run a basic credit check. Payment terms post-pilot revert to Net45 unless otherwise agreed in a future amendment.
- Sample invoice/remittance: attached (sample_invoice_PulseHealth.csv) — please share the AP system field mapping and we will adapt.

If PulseHealth confirms they will provide two trade references within 7 business days we will commit to an initial $300k cap. Otherwise we will proceed with $250k and aim to review at the 90-day checkpoint.

Next steps: Lena, if you can confirm trade refs or upload the deposit receipt to the DocuSign envelope, I’ll get finance to sign off and route the MSA for execution.

Best regards,

Jordan Blake
